sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Mableton
sections.html:
Mableton sellers can list with an agent, handle the sale alone, or take an as-is offer. Weigh the cost of repairs against the date you need to move. A listing reaches buyers who rely on mortgages and works best on a house that shows well. A private sale keeps the agent's share but puts pricing, showings and contracts on you. A cash buyer takes the house in its present condition and skips the lender's appraisal.

Get every offer's terms in writing, including who pays the state transfer tax and how the county and city tax bills will be settled at closing.

Mableton is a south Cobb County community that voted for cityhood on November 8, 2022, and elected its first council on March 21, 2023. The 2025 estimate is 78,820 people, up from 77,077 in April 2020. Of 29,109 households, 64.6 percent own their homes. The median home is worth $313,100, owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,777 a month, and gross rent runs about $1,472.

Nearly nine in ten residents stayed at the same address for a year, so many sellers on established streets have owned for a long time. With this many people and plenty of competing listings, condition and price matter most. Price against what is actually for sale on your street.

Mableton lies about 15 miles west-northwest of Atlanta and about 20 miles from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. The Silver Comet Trail, a 61.5-mile paved path that starts in Smyrna, crosses Floyd Road in Mableton, and a buyer who works nearby or toward Smyrna may value that commute more than new finishes.

Fulton County Airport, known as Brown Field, touches Mableton's southeast border. It has two runways and about 65,000 operations a year, so a house on that side may hear aircraft. Expect buyers to ask.

Cobb County's school district runs the public schools. Elementary schools in the area include Mableton, Clay-Harmony Leland, Bryant, Riverside, Russell and City View. Pebblebrook and South Cobb are the high schools. Assignment follows the address, so check it with the district before you name a school in your listing.

County planning documents describe a Mableton Town Center vision for the Mableton Parkway area, approved by the Cobb Board of Commissioners in 2013. Later projects include a 31-acre mixed-use plaza near Mableton Parkway and Old Powder Springs Road with townhomes, courtyard cottages and detached houses, and a 60-acre redevelopment along Floyd Road with apartments and townhomes, approved on October 21, 2020.

New construction nearby can raise buyer interest in the area, and it also gives buyers newer alternatives. Treat it as a reason to price carefully, not as a selling point you can quantify.

sections.h2: Who bills what: Cobb County and the city
sections.html:
The city has no general property tax. Cobb County keeps billing county and school taxes, and Mableton sends separate bills for its special service districts. The county assessor values property at 40 percent of market and mails notices in early summer. Cobb bills go out in August and are due October 15.

The city's Public Safety Special Services District covers police services the city took over from Cobb on June 1, 2025. The city began billing it in October 2026 at 4.5 mills, applied to the assessed value set by Cobb. A separate Six Flags Special Services District has been billed by the city since October 2025.

Ask your closing attorney or the title company to pull the Cobb bill and each city district bill, since a buyer will want to know how every one was settled. Your sales contract decides who pays which share of the year.

The city applies its millage to the assessed value Cobb sets. Ask the city finance office for the district bill's due date, and keep proof of payment for the closing file. The state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant appears as a separate reduction on eligible Cobb bills, and anyone who loses homestead eligibility must tell the Tax Commissioner.

The homestead exemption is a break for owners who live in the house as a primary residence. Cobb's assessor sets a filing deadline each July. An owner who is no longer eligible must report it before the appeal deadline or owe the back taxes and interest, plus a 50 percent penalty on the amount wrongly reduced.

After a sale, make sure the Tax Commissioner and your closing attorney know the house stopped being your primary residence at transfer.

Mableton's Building Division reviews plans against Georgia's minimum standard codes, inspects work and issues Certificates of Occupancy. Applications go through the online CloudPermit portal only, and emailed ones are refused. Crews may work 7 AM to 7 PM weekdays and 9 AM to 5 PM Saturdays, never on Sundays or designated holidays.

  • Collect permits and final inspection records for recent work.
  • Ask the general contractor to confirm each inspection passed.
  • If the home was rented, ask the city's Business License office whether any registration is still active.

A house in poor repair can still be sold as is, to a buyer who accepts the condition. Keep permit records for earlier work so title review does not stall the closing.

The state's transfer tax is printed as $1 for the first $1,000 of price, or fractional part of $1,000, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. Your contract may shift it to the buyer. Either way, the deed cannot be recorded with the court clerk until the tax is paid.

1. The deed and your mortgage payoff details.
  2. The latest Cobb tax bill and any city district bill.
  3. Permit and final inspection records for recent work.
  4. Any notice about a pending value appeal, because it changes the bill a buyer will see.

With these in one folder, an agent can answer a buyer's questions the same day, and a cash buyer can make a firm offer without waiting on records. A sale that runs through a lender also moves faster when the tax bills and permit history are already in hand, since the title company asks for them early.

Talk to the closing attorney before you sign, so the contract says plainly who is responsible for each charge that falls between the first of January and the closing date.

faqs.q: Does Mableton levy a city property tax?
faqs.a: There is no general city levy. Mableton bills a Public Safety district at 4.5 mills, which began in October 2026, and a Six Flags district it has billed since October 2025. Cobb still bills county and school taxes.

faqs.q: When are Cobb property taxes due for Mableton owners?
faqs.a: October 15 each year. The payment must reach the Tax Commissioner's Office or be postmarked by USPS that day.

faqs.q: How long can I contest my Cobb value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date printed on the Notice of Assessment. A parcel with an appeal pending receives a temporary bill at 85 percent of assessed value until it is settled.

faqs.q: Who sets property values inside Mableton?
faqs.a: Cobb County. Values come from the Cobb assessor, and appeals go to the Cobb Board of Tax Assessors, which also oversees homestead filings.

faqs.q: Can a Mableton house in poor repair be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, as is, to a buyer who accepts the condition, or after fixes through a listing. Keep permit records for earlier work so title review does not stall the closing.
